card: This PR refactors HTTPRemoteClient disconnection logic by flattening the control flow into a const ShouldDisconnect method, adding a debug log when non-keep-alive connections close, and switching idle tracking to a mockable steady clock. It adds unit test coverage for idle timeouts, slow sends, shutdown disconnections, and malformed requests. The change addresses review feedback from the recent libevent removal and follow-up HTTP server refactors.
changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the implementation; metadata references to downstream PRs were removed.
evidence: PR description notes #35182 had one case flagging a client for disconnect without logging the reason.
PR description cites PR #35829 review discussion (#35829#discussion_r3846342291) regarding complex control flow and lack of unit tests in MaybeDisconnect.
problem: Following the replacement of libevent with a custom HTTP server, HTTPRemoteClient::MaybeDisconnect was non-const, lacked unit tests, had complex nested control flow, missed logging for one disconnect path, and could log misleading idle timeouts for connections already marked for disconnect.

risk.why: A flaw in HTTP client disconnect logic could prematurely terminate active RPC connections or fail to disconnect idle connections during shutdown.

scope_notes: The diff includes a unit test using mock socket primitives to exercise HTTP client idle timeouts and shutdown behavior.
summary: Refactors HTTPRemoteClient disconnection handling by replacing MaybeDisconnect with a const ShouldDisconnect method and flattening its conditional branches. It switches client idle timeout tracking to MockableSteadyClock to enable deterministic testing and adds comprehensive unit tests covering timeout and disconnect cases. It also adds a missing debug log when a non-keep-alive client completes its reply.
